subject: Cloud Computing
title: Cloud and the Environment
description: A quick win: understand Cloud and the Environment.

hook.text: Data centers use 1–2% of the world's electricity — more than some entire countries.

buildup.text: Cooling servers generates enormous heat. Early data centers wasted most energy on cooling.

discovery.text: Cloud providers are now the largest corporate buyers of renewable energy on Earth.

twist.text: Moving to the cloud actually cuts emissions. Shared infrastructure is more efficient overall.

climax.text: Google claims carbon neutrality since 2007. Microsoft pledged carbon negative by 2030.

punchline.text: The cloud has a carbon footprint. But it's shrinking.

quiz.question: How does moving to the cloud affect carbon emissions?
options: It typically reduces emissions because shared infrastructure is more efficient
It always increases emissions due to massive data center energy use
It has no effect on carbon emissions whatsoever

details.summary: Cloud computing's environmental impact is complex. Cloud data centers are more energy-efficient than on-premises alternatives, but the total scale of cloud computing consumes enormous amounts of electricity and water. Major providers have committed to renewable energy goals.
details.whyItMatters: As cloud usage grows, its environmental footprint becomes a critical societal concern. Understanding the trade-offs helps organizations make informed decisions about sustainability.
takeaways: Cloud data centers are more efficient than typical on-premises servers
The total energy consumption of cloud is still enormous
Major providers commit to 100% renewable energy goals

faq.question: Is cloud computing good or bad for the environment?
faq.answer: Cloud consolidation improves efficiency compared to millions of underutilized on-premises servers. However, cloud enables more total computing, increasing absolute energy consumption. The net effect depends on whether efficiency gains outpace demand growth.

faq.question: What are cloud providers doing about sustainability?
faq.answer: AWS aims for 100 percent renewable energy by 2025. Google has been carbon neutral since 2007 and targets 24/7 carbon-free energy by 2030. Microsoft committed to being carbon negative by 2030. All three invest heavily in renewable energy projects.
